subject: [PATCH 2/2] mm/gup: batch contiguous PTE-mapped large folios in follow_page_mask()

reviews.author: David (Arm)
reviews.summary:
Reviewer David (Arm) requested that comments be removed from the patch and instead placed directly in the function where they are relevant, specifically mentioning that gup_must_unshare() logic should be above its usage.

Reviewer David (Arm) pointed out that the 'page' parameter in folio_pte_batch_flags() is not used, and suggested using an existing helper function page_anon_exclusive_batch() from mm/mprotect.c to handle this case.

Reviewer noted that folio_pte_batch_flags() is only required for anonymous folios and suggested an optimization to check the folio type after counting contiguous PTEs, returning early if it's not anonymous or a single page, and then calling page_anon_exclusive_batch() with care about gup_must_unshare().
reviews.raw_body:
Drop all of these comments and rather comment in the function on the important
bits. For example, the gup_must_unshare() logic belongs above the relevant code
below. If we cannot easily sort it out.

---

Why pass the "page" when it is not even used?

Maybe it should be used? :)

In mm/mprotect.c we do have a page_anon_exclusive_batch() helper already that
would do the right thing. See below.

---

This is really only required for anonymous folios, though.

So likely you could instead just do after the folio_pte_batch_flags() a

nr = folio_pte_batch_flags() ...
if (nr == 1 || !folio_test_anon(folio) || pte_write(pte))
	return nr;
/* Careful with gup_must_unshare(). */
return page_anon_exclusive_batch(0, nr, page, PageAnonExclusive(page));
	

I'll note that the page_anon_exclusive_batch() helper is rather ugly, maybe
you'd just want a nicer one local to this function. It's pretty small in the
end, so you might also just open code a simple loop over PageAnonExclusive().

2026-07-29.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the handling of PTE-mapped large folios in the Linux kernel's memory management system. Currently, follow_page_mask() returns one page per call for a PTE-mapped large folio, leading to inefficient re-walking of page tables. The patch introduces a new function, folio_pte_batch_flags(), which counts consecutive present PTEs mapping contiguous pages with uniform write bits. This allows the kernel to batch contiguous runs of pages in one step, improving performance for large anonymous regions. The patch also maintains per-PTE guarantees and ensures that writable runs are safe for any access, while read-only runs are only batched for plain reads.
